stem: A 60-year-old woman comes to the clinic due to worsening dyspepsia and unintentional weight loss over the past 3 months.  Vital signs are normal.  Abdominal examination shows mild epigastric tenderness.  CT scan of the abdomen reveals gastric mucosal thickening but no evidence of abdominal lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly.  Endoscopy shows nodular gastric folds, and biopsy shows proliferation of small, clonal, mucosa-associated B cells expressing the CD20 antigen.  Which of the following microbial mechanisms is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's findings?​‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌​‌‌​​​​‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌

options.label: E
options.text: Integration of microbial genome into host genome

explanation:
This patient's gastric nodules composed of small clonal B cells are indicative of an extranodal marginal zone lymphoma involving mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma).  This form of non-Hodgkin lymphoma arises from post–germinal center marginal zone B cells and expresses pan–B-cell markers (eg, CD19, CD20) while lacking CD5 and CD10, distinguishing it from mantle cell and follicular lymphoma.

The normal gastric mucosa contains no organized lymphoid tissue; MALT arises only in response to chronic antigen exposure from bacterial, viral, or autoimmune sources.  The most common trigger for gastric MALT lymphoma is Helicobacter pylori infection, which leads to local recruitment and proliferation of antigen-specific T and B lymphocytes.  Over time, chronic immune stimulation results in the emergence of a monoclonal B-cell line that proliferates excessively in the presence of H pylori antigens.  This cell line eventually accumulates genetic abnormalities that allow it to proliferate in an antigen-independent fashion, resulting in spread away from the local site of infection.

Because most cases of gastric MALT lymphoma are tightly linked to H pylori infection, antimicrobial treatment can often result in complete remission of early-stage disease due to elimination of the bacterial antigens driving tumor proliferation.

(Choices B and E)  Certain human papillomavirus (HPV) types cause epithelial cancers (eg, oropharynx, cervix, anus).  HPV integration into the host genome removes the viral controls that normally limit expression of oncoproteins E6 and E7.  E6 causes degradation of host p53 protein, a mediator of DNA damage repair and negative regulator of the cell cycle, which accelerates malignant transformation.

(Choice C)  Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a lymphotropic, oncogenic virus associated with certain B- and T-cell lymphomas.  In latent EBV infection, episomal EBV DNA generates low levels of viral proteins that allow it to evade the host immune response.  The viral proteins also activate proliferation-promoting and antiapoptotic host genes, leading to oncogenesis in a minority of cases.

(Choice D)  Somatic hypermutation of the immunoglobulin variable region generates high-affinity antibodies during B-cell maturation in the germinal center.  MALT lymphoma cells show evidence of having completed this normal process, but hypermutation itself does not drive their proliferation.

Educational objective:Helicobacter pylori is associated with gastric MALT lymphoma due to chronic stimulation of the immune response; the continuous cell division predisposes to accumulation of mutations that result in aberrant B-cell proliferation.  Treatment of H pylori can induce remission in most early-stage cases.​‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌​‌‌​​​​‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​‌​​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌
